title: Uruguayan permanent residence for nationals of Mercosur member and associated states

sources.title: Ley N.º 18.250, article 33, literal B, as worded by Ley N.º 20.075: permanent residence for nationals of the Mercosur States Parties and Associated States who prove that nationality
Ley N.º 18.250, article 33, last paragraphs: the application goes to the Ministry of the Interior or a consulate, and the Ministry decides within 90 business days
Ley N.º 20.075, article 169: the current wording of article 33 of Ley N.º 18.250 applies from 120 days after the law's promulgation on 2022-10-20
Ley N.º 18.250, article 10: family reunification with parents, spouses, partners (concubinos), and unmarried children who are minors or adults with a disability
Ley N.º 18.250, article 45, literals B to D, as first worded, to 2023-12-31: crimes against humanity, an expulsion or re-entry ban not revoked, a conviction for trafficking, laundering, drugs or arms
Ley N.º 18.250, article 46, as first worded, to 2023-12-31: residence is denied after a prosecution or conviction for an intentional common crime with over two years of prison under Uruguayan law
Decreto N.º 45/023, article 2: a valid passport or identity document, and for applicants over 18 a sworn statement that articles 45, B to D, and 46 of Ley N.º 18.250 do not apply
Decreto N.º 45/023, article 8: the procedure follows the reciprocity agreement between Uruguay and the applicant's state
Ley N.º 17.927, Mercosur Residence Agreements, article 2: the States Parties are Mercosur members and associated states; a naturalized national counts after five years
Ley N.º 17.927, Mercosur Residence Agreements, article 9.2: family members without a party's nationality get a residence of the same term as the person they depend on
Ley N.º 17.927, Residence Agreement for nationals of the Mercosur States Parties, Bolivia and Chile, opening: its parties are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Bolivia and Chile
Dirección Nacional de Migración, Residencia legal: Mercosur permanent residence for nationals of AR, BO, BR, CL, CO, EC, GY, PE, PY, SR and VE
Dirección Nacional de Migración, Residencia Legal Permanente Mercosur: requirements, minors, fees in indexed units, and no fee for Brazilians and Paraguayans by reciprocity
Ley N.º 18.246 (unión concubinaria), article 1: the rights of a stable union arise after at least five years of uninterrupted living together
Decreto N.º 394/009 (regulation of Ley N.º 18.250), article 16: a stable union is proved only by its registered judicial recognition
Civil Code, article 280: majority is reached at 18 completed years, and parental authority also ends with a child's marriage
Decreto N.º 45/023, article 2, literals c and d: criminal record certificates of each country lived in for over six months in the last five years, and the Uruguayan vaccination scheme certificate
Decreto N.º 45/023, article 4: a consulate’s certificate lets the applicant enter as a resident in process, with 30 business days after entry to complete the papers at the directorate

requirements.title: Holds the nationality of a Mercosur member or associated state: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname or Venezuela

assessments.title: No prosecution or conviction for an intentional common crime with over two years of prison under Uruguayan law, nor repeated offending, unless five years passed since the sentence with no new crime
No crime against humanity, no conviction for trafficking, laundering, drugs or arms, and no expulsion or re-entry ban not revoked
Criminal record certificates, at national level, of each country lived in for more than six months in the last five years; applicants under 18 do not present them
A valid certificate, issued by a vaccination centre in Uruguay, that the applicant meets the Uruguayan vaccination scheme
Original, valid papers: photo, ID or passport, any marriage certificate under a year old; foreign papers apostilled or legalized, unless verifiable online, and translated, save Brazil’s
Under 18: birth certificate legalized or apostilled, and express consent of the parents with parental authority, in person or by a power notarized in Uruguay, valid 180 days
Apply to the Ministry of the Interior (online, then in person) or at a Uruguayan consulate, then complete within 30 business days of entry; the decision is due within 90 business days
Fees in indexed units (UI), readjusted every six months: residence 557.30 UI, none for Brazilians and Paraguayans; certificate 55.70 UI; a 225.60 UI re-entry permit per exit while pending

dependents.title: Spouse who depends on a principal from Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile or Paraguay; others: possible
Partner of five years or more, who counts only once a court has recognised the union and the ruling is registered, which is not recorded: possible
Unmarried children under 18 who depend on a principal from Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile or Paraguay; adults only with a disability, which is not recorded: possible
The spouse's unmarried children, whom article 10 of the migration law does not name, so they count only as family members under the agreements, which is not settled: possible
Parents who depend on a principal from Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile or Paraguay; others: possible
